input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 only lets either Party stop the annual auto-renewal on ninety (90) days' written notice, so the Company has no mid-term convenience right, and Section 4.2(a) imposes a Termination Payment of 50% of trailing twelve-month Net Sales above $800,000 (payable in eight quarterly instalments) on any Company termination. That is an uncapped exit penalty running to many multiples of three months' Section 3.1 fees (30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month), so the clause fails the fallback on a material term. We take the fallback: an express Customer convenience right on 90 days' written notice, with the Termination Payment capped at the payments made to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date. HDI's convenience right already sits at the fallback, being exercisable only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days written notice to HDI; for purposes of this Section 4.1, "Customer" means the Company.

ops.newText: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two; provided, that the Termination Payment shall not exceed the payments made to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an express right for the Company (as Customer) to terminate for convenience on 90 days' written notice, and capped the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments, which is the maximum early-termination fee our playbook permits.
proposal.summary: Add an express Customer convenience termination right on 90 days' notice and cap the Termination Payment at three months' Section 3.1 payments.
